title: dispatch, run and session across projects
acceptance: fm-dispatch.sh and fm-run.sh take --project, read that project's task list from the registry, resolve depends_on within the project and pass --project to every script they call. The concurrency limit stays one global number across all projects. Dispatch to a non-default project runs fm-project.sh verify first and dispatches nothing on its refusal.

Revised by firstmate on 2026-09-24 at the captain's instruction, before any work started, to match what has since been decided or merged: T-059 made fm-dispatch.sh start only tasks that fm-ready.sh lists as cleared (judged, and answered A on the task's own choice card). Across projects, readiness, judgments and clearance are keyed by (project, task), so clearing T-012 in one project never clears T-012 in another. The fair fill of design.md §15.10 point 2 chooses among cleared tasks only. Tests with two registered projects cover both.
The greenlit check matches the project: a greenlit event for one project authorizes nothing in another. fm-session.sh status reports live work grouped by project.

Implements the script half of design.md section 15.10 (points 1-3). Live runs are counted by (project, task) across every project against the one global limit, under a dispatch slot lock held only while fm-dispatch.sh recounts live runs, takes free slots and emits dispatched, so two dispatches started at once never exceed the limit; fm-project.sh verify, the task lists and the greenlit check run before the lock is taken. fm-dispatch.sh with no --project fills free slots across every registered project one at a time, each to the project with a ready, greenlit, verified task and the fewest live runs, ties to the name that sorts first, and with only the default project registered behaves exactly as today; --project dispatches only that project within the same limit and lock. fm-run.sh notes the project's base commit before gating and, under a per-project lock, requests a merge card only when that project's merge turn is free and base is still that commit; the turn is freed by a send back or hold, and for a merge only once the decision record's merge outcome is merged or failed, never on the answer alone. Otherwise it requests none and says whether the card waits for a pending or running merge or for a regate on the new base; a merge card or merge in one project never holds back another project's.

Tests with two registered projects live at the same time, written to fail first: runs in both projects are in flight together up to the limit and a shared task id in both is counted twice, not once; two concurrent dispatch calls never exceed the limit; dispatch with no --project splits free slots fairly and hands a freed slot to the project with fewer live runs; with a merge card pending in one project, fm-run.sh requests a merge card in the other project but not a second one in the first; with a merge answered but its outcome not yet recorded, fm-run.sh still requests no second card in that project, and once base has moved it requests none for a branch gated against the old base.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Count actual live owned rounds under dispatch and identity allocation locks, not historical events or open PR counts. Recover stale reservations from owner completion; same task ID in two projects consumes separate slots. Private events/decisions stay in project state; board aggregation exposes authorized metadata only. Dynamic summaries carry en and zh-TW.
